The later paper (Streaming Knowledge Compilation / Online WiCER) extends WiCER's CEGAR-inspired loop by replacing reactive, probe-driven pinning with proactive pinning driven by a predicted materiality signal [2606.09877#s2.p3][2605.07068#s37.p1].

From reactive to proactive: In WiCER the loop is reactive—the wiki is evaluated against diagnostic probes, and any probe scoring 1/5 triggers diagnosis of dropped facts that are then pinned as preservation constraints [2605.07068#s36.p1]. Online WiCER removes the static-corpus assumption and instead pins facts before any query exposes a gap, using a bounded materiality signal φ_t(k,n)∈[0,1] as a query-relevance surrogate [2606.09877#s2.p3][2606.09877#s2.p2]. Queries cannot drive pinning because they arrive after the news batch [2606.09877#s19.p2]. The loop becomes: mine candidate facts, score marginal value with a state-aware scorer, pin greedily under budget with decay-weighted eviction, and compile incrementally with periodic full recompilation [2606.09877#s2.p5].

Key conceptual shift in the 'counterexample': the paper formalizes predictive CEGAR—the counterexample is no longer an observed QA failure (a score-1 probe) but a predicted high-materiality news item [2606.09877#s42.p1][2606.09877#s42.p4]. Refinement thus shifts from diagnosis to prediction [2606.09877#s42.p1]. This introduces prediction error ε=E[|φ_t−φ̂_t|] as the only domain-specific quantity, yielding regret O(√(T log K)) + O(B_miss·T·ε) [2606.09877#s43.p3][2606.09877#s15.p1].

respuesta: Agent Zero Memory treats knowledge updates epistemically: it records assertions with origin, immutable timestamp, and evidence pointers (provenanced items), and answers are citation-locked so every claim must be supported by an opened item or the reader returns ⊥, structurally excluding fabrication [2608.29606#s6.p2][2608.29606#s6.p3][2608.29606#s6.p4]. respuesta: WiCER's loop is reactive: it evaluates the compiled wiki with one diagnostic probe per source document, and any probe scoring 1/5 triggers diagnosis of the dropped facts, which are fed back as preservation constraints—i.e., CEGAR where the document collection is the concrete system, the wiki the abstraction, a score-1 probe the counterexample, and pinning the refinement [2605.07068#s37.p1][2605.07068#s36.p1]. Streaming Knowledge Compilation (Online WiCER) removes the static-corpus assumption and replaces this reactive, probe-driven pinning with proactive pinning driven by a predicted materiality signal φ̂_t, adding decay-weighted eviction and periodic full recompilation every T_r steps [2606.09877#s2.p3][2606.09877#s31.p2]. Because queries arrive only after the news batch, they cannot drive pinning; instead a bounded materiality signal φ_t(k,n)∈[0,1] scores a document's importance for an entity and serves as a query-relevance surrogate, so facts are pinned before any query exposes a gap [2606.09877#s19.p2][2606.09877#s2.p3]. The key conceptual shift is formalized as *predictive CEGAR*: the counterexample is no longer an observed QA failure (a score-1 probe) but a predicted high-materiality news item, shifting refinement from diagnosis to prediction [2606.09877#s42.p1][2606.09877#s42.p4]. Prediction error ε=E[|φ_t−φ̂_t|] becomes the only domain-specific quantity in the regret bound O(√(T log K)) + O(B_miss·T·ε) [2606.09877#s43.p3][2606.09877#s15.p1].
